title: follow-through secondary motion spec
description: What moves on its own on one object, and how. Written by follow-through in Blender as the object custom property `follow_through`, carried by glTF as node extras (export_extras=True), and read in Godot 4.7 as node.get_meta("extras")["follow_through"]. glTF numbers arrive in Godot as floats, so every integer field below must be accepted as a whole-valued float.

schema.description: Version of this contract. A reader refuses a spec whose major version it does not know.

family.description: The dimension of what moves. strand: 1D (rope, tail, hair). shell: 2D surface (cloth, flag, sail). volume: 3D body with an inside (jello, flesh).

class.description: How it hangs and what holds it. hanging_sheet: held along an edge by a static or moving prop (flag, banner, curtain). draped_sheet: worn and held along its top edge (cape, cloak). draped_tube: worn, open at both ends, held by one ring (skirt, robe). loose_sheet: held by nothing, rests on things (tablecloth, towel). strap: a strip long enough to move as a strand (scarf, ribbon). tensioned: held at corners and pulled taut (sail, awning). solid_sheet: cloth modelled with thickness - not simulable as a surface. volume / not_cloth: recognised and declined.

route.description: The Godot runtime that moves it. soft_body: SoftBody3D. spring_bones: SpringBoneSimulator3D on a bone chain. none: nothing moves.

guessed.description: Which decisions had no geometric evidence behind them. A consumer may warn on these.

object.description: Blender object name at the time of writing.

vertices.description: Blender vertex count. glTF will have more wherever UV seams split vertices.

pin_group.description: Blender vertex group that is the editable source of the pins.

areal_density_gsm.description: Grams per square metre - how fabric weight is sold. total_mass is this times area.

soft_body.description: SoftBody3D properties, named exactly as Godot 4.7 names them. Under Jolt these must be set BEFORE the node enters the tree: set afterwards, linear_stiffness, simulation_precision and shrinking_factor are silently ignored.

simulation_precision.description: Integer. Jolt substeps per physics tick.

damping_coefficient.description: A velocity decay rate per second, not a fraction: values above 1 are accepted and act (measured). Terminal fall speed is gravity / this.

pins.description: Which points are held, and by what. Carried as positions, not vertex indices: Godot's importer reorders vertices and UV seams split them, so an index from Blender names the wrong point. Every Godot vertex within `tolerance` of a listed position is pinned, which also pins both halves of a seam.

space.description: Vertex coordinates exactly as the glTF file holds them, which are Godot's ArrayMesh vertex positions. Blender (x, y, z) becomes (x, z, -y). For an unskinned mesh these are mesh-local. For a skinned mesh the exporter bakes the object's world transform into the vertices, so they are Blender world coordinates converted the same way.

positions.description: Flat [x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, ...], length 3 * count. Flat because nested arrays are not a safe Blender custom property.

anchor.description: What a pinned point follows. node: the imported mesh node's transform - static if it is static, carried if its parents move (a flag on a ship). bone: the bone named per pin in `bones` (a cape). none: no pins.

bones.description: With anchor=bone: the bone each pin follows, one per pin, in the same order as positions. The strongest deform weight on that vertex in Blender.

touching.description: Blender names of objects the cloth touched when recognised. Informational: a Godot scene decides its own colliders.
